- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.11 to +0.17) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.22 to -0.28) — model fails to fully account for bearish momentum.
- Lag in correction: model often delays downward adjustments after negative sentiment, especially if recent prices are high.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, pushing prices too far from recent mean — especially in 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to overfit recent trends, ignoring longer-term mean or seasonal patterns.
- Overshoots after positive sentiment spikes — model assumes momentum will continue, but sentiment often corrects within 3–5 days.
- Avoid extrapolating from 18-day history — model overfits recent data, especially when sentiment is volatile or trending.
